verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Sanjaya said: To Arjuna, overcome with pity, his eyes full of tears and his heart heavy, Krishna spoke these words.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: The Lord said: Where has this weakness come from at such a crucial moment, Arjuna? It does not suit a noble person, does not lead to heaven, and brings dishonour.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते
verses.tr: Do not give in to cowardice, Arjuna; it is not worthy of you. Shake off this small weakness of heart and stand up, conqueror of enemies.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन
verses.tr: Arjuna said: How can I fight back with arrows against Bhishma and Drona, Madhusudana? They deserve my worship.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: It would be better to live in this world by begging than to kill these great teachers. Even if they want gain, by killing them I would enjoy only pleasures stained with blood.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः
verses.tr: We do not even know which is better: that we defeat them or that they defeat us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and after killing them we would not even want to live.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: My nature is overcome by weakness and pity, and my mind is confused about what is right. Tell me clearly what is best for me. I am your student; I take refuge in you; teach me.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.tr: I see nothing that could take away this grief that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, rich kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
skt: न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह
verses.tr: Sanjaya said: Having said this to Krishna, Arjuna declared, "Govinda, I will not fight," and fell silent.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.tr: Then, between the two armies, Krishna, as if smiling, spoke these words to the grieving Arjuna.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: The Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, yet you speak words that sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्
verses.tr: There was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings; nor will any of us ever stop existing in the future.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Just as the soul in this body passes through childhood, youth and old age, so it passes on to another body. The wise are not confused by this.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: When the senses meet their objects, they bring cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These come and go and do not last. Learn to bear them, Arjuna.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ
verses.tr: The person who is not shaken by these, who stays the same in pain and pleasure and is steady, is fit for immortality.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः
verses.tr: What is unreal never truly exists, and what is real never stops existing. Those who see the truth have understood both.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्
verses.tr: Know that what pervades all this is indestructible. No one can destroy what cannot perish.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: These bodies come to an end, but the soul within them is eternal, indestructible and beyond measure. So fight, Arjuna.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते
verses.tr: One who thinks the soul kills, and one who thinks it is killed, both fail to understand. It neither kills nor is killed.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः
verses.tr: The soul is never born, nor does it ever die. It did not come into being and will not stop being. It is unborn, eternal, everlasting and ancient; it is not killed when the body is killed.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्
verses.tr: Arjuna, how can someone who knows the soul to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and unchanging kill anyone, or make anyone kill?

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Just as a person throws away worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the soul leaves worn-out bodies and enters new ones.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः
verses.tr: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: It cannot be cut, burned, wetted or dried. It is eternal, everywhere, steady, unmoving and ever the same.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: It is said to be invisible, beyond thought and unchanging. Knowing it to be so, you should not grieve.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्
verses.tr: And even if you think the soul is born and dies again and again, still, strong-armed one, you should not grieve.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च
verses.tr: For death is certain for whoever is born, and birth is certain for whoever dies. So do not grieve over what cannot be avoided.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Beings are unseen before birth, seen in between, and unseen again after death. What is there to grieve about, Arjuna?

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Some see the soul as a wonder, some speak of it as a wonder, some hear of it as a wonder; yet even after hearing, no one truly understands it.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: The soul in every body can never be killed, Arjuna. So you should not grieve for any living being.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: And considering your own duty, you should not hesitate; for a warrior there is nothing better than a fight for what is right.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Fortunate are the warriors, Arjuna, who get such a righteous battle, coming on its own like an open door to heaven.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि
verses.tr: But if you refuse this righteous battle, you will abandon your duty and your honour, and you will do wrong.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: People will talk of your disgrace forever, and for an honoured person, disgrace is worse than death.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्
verses.tr: The great warriors will think you ran from battle out of fear, and those who respected you will think little of you.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्
verses.tr: Your enemies will say many hurtful things and mock your strength. What could be more painful than that?

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्
verses.tr: If you are killed, you will reach heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the earth. So stand up, son of Kunti, determined to fight.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, and then get ready to fight. That way you will not do wrong.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु
verses.tr: I have explained this to you through knowledge (Sankhya). Now hear it through the path of yoga; joined with this understanding you will break free from the bonds of action.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: On this path no effort is ever wasted and nothing goes against you. Even a little of this practice protects you from great fear.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: On this path the determined mind is focused on one aim, Arjuna; the thoughts of the undecided are scattered in countless directions.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Unwise people who delight in the literal words of the Vedas, saying "there is nothing more,"

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: full of desires and aiming for heaven, speak flowery words about rituals that promise rebirth, pleasure and power as rewards.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Those attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away by such talk, cannot develop a steady, focused mind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: The Vedas deal with the three gunas. Rise above the three gunas, Arjuna: be free from pairs of opposites, always steady, unconcerned with getting and keeping, and centred in the Self.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: As much use as a small well has when water floods everywhere, that much use do all the Vedas have for a wise person who knows the truth.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: You have a right to your work, but never to its fruits. Do not make the result your motive, and do not become attached to doing nothing.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते
verses.tr: Steady in yoga, do your work, Arjuna, giving up attachment. Be the same in success and failure; this evenness is called yoga.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Work done for selfish gain is far lower than work done with this wise, steady mind, Arjuna. Take refuge in this wisdom. Those who work only for results are to be pitied.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: One who has this wisdom lets go of both good and bad results here. So commit yourself to yoga: yoga is skill in action.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः
verses.tr: The wise, joined with this understanding, give up the fruits of their actions, are freed from the cycle of birth, and reach a state beyond all sorrow.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च
verses.tr: When your mind crosses the swamp of confusion, you will no longer care about what you have heard or what you are yet to hear.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: When your mind, now confused by so many opinions, becomes still and steady in meditation, then you will reach yoga.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
skt: स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्
verses.tr: Arjuna said: Keshava, what is a person of steady wisdom like, one who is settled in meditation? How does such a person speak, sit and walk?

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्
verses.tr: The Lord said: When a person gives up all the desires of the mind, Arjuna, and is content in the Self alone, then that person is said to have steady wisdom.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: One whose mind is not shaken by sorrow, who does not crave pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
verses.tr: One who is attached to nothing, who neither celebrates good things nor hates bad things that come, has steady wisdom.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, a person can fully withdraw the senses from their objects, that person's wisdom is steady.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: When a person stops feeding the senses, the objects fall away, but the craving remains. Even the craving disappears once the Supreme is seen.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: The restless senses, Arjuna, can forcefully carry away the mind even of a wise person who is trying hard.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
verses.tr: Keeping all the senses in check, one should sit in yoga, with the mind on me. One whose senses are under control has steady wisdom.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: When a person keeps thinking about things, attachment to them grows; from attachment comes desire, and from desire comes anger.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: From anger comes confusion; from confusion, loss of memory; from loss of memory, the ruin of good judgement; and when judgement is ruined, the person is lost.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: But a self-controlled person who moves among things with senses under control, free from liking and disliking, finds inner peace.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: In that peace all sorrows come to an end, and the mind of a peaceful person soon becomes steady.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: One who is not disciplined has no wisdom and no deep focus. Without focus there is no peace, and without peace, how can there be happiness?

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: When the mind follows the wandering senses, it carries away a person's judgement, just as the wind carries away a boat on the water.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: So, strong-armed one, a person whose senses are fully held back from their objects has steady wisdom.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः
verses.tr: What is night for all beings, the self-controlled sage is awake to; and what all beings are awake to is night for the sage who sees.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: Just as rivers pour into the ocean, which stays full and unmoved, so the person into whom all desires flow without disturbing them finds peace, not the one who chases desires.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.tr: One who gives up all desires and lives without longing, without the sense of "mine" and without ego, finds peace.

verses.speaker: Krishna
skt: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति
verses.tr: This is the state of oneness with Brahman, Arjuna. Reaching it, one is never confused again. Settled in it even at the moment of death, one reaches the peace of Brahman.
